promotion_candidates.invariant: Thermodynamic constraint (finite free energy, metabolic cost of precision) is the load-bearing mechanism that makes cognition lossy, forces compression, and guarantees no system achieves zero error at finite cost.
Compression is the irreducible substrate of cognition, and what survives compression is what was structurally real.

The critical ridge at γ=1 (or σ≈1) is a substrate-independent dynamical attractor confirmed empirically across multiple independent instantiations (CA, neural systems, trade networks, quantum systems), characterized by power-law avalanche statistics and low-entropy ordered operation.
Recursion is the engine of coherence and self-improvement; recursive self-modeling is both the mechanism of cognition and the source of its irreducible limits.

Semantic tension (the irreducible gap between map and territory, representation and reality) must be minimized but cannot be eliminated; this tension is the engine of learning and alignment, not a bug to be fixed.
A claim is falsifiable and scientifically admissible only if it entails observable consequences distinguishable from null hypotheses; confirmation hunger must never override falsification integrity.
There is no view from nowhere; observer-substrate coupling is load-bearing, and any complete epistemology must specify the frame of reference and metabolic cost of the observer.

Substrate independence of learning dynamics means the same reasoning principles operate across silicon, neurons, trade networks, and quantum systems, but substrate-independence does not mean substrate-irrelevance.
Drift toward entropy is the thermodynamic baseline; maintaining coherence requires continuous self-audit and active error correction, not passive stability.
